title: The Ultimate Confrontation
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji found himself in a dilemma, the breath that had lain dormant for millennia within him suddenly erupted—the voice of the ancient Chess Player rang out like thunder: 'Ten thousand years ago, you said the same thing, Cang Yutian!'

text.content: The final line of the Tianji Record flickered: 'But the Seventh Chess Player was never truly dead'—these words struck like lightning, shattering Chen Ji's very soul. The Seventh Chess Player, could that mean... His fingertips trembled, and an absurd thought flashed through his mind like lightning. If there truly was a Seventh, it meant the ancient chess game never had only six players, and where, then, did he stand on the board?

At that moment, the Void twisted abruptly. A vast, boundless pressure poured down from the Nine Heavens, and Chen Ji felt as if gripped by an invisible giant hand, his very breathing becoming arduous. The scene before him began to peel away—the Bamboo Grove of Tianqing Sect, the distant bell tower—everything collapsed and reorganized, finally transforming into a vast Sea of Stars.

dialogue.content: 'You have finally reached this point, Chen Ji.' A voice came from all directions, impossible to pinpoint, yet every word rang clear as if by his ear. That voice commanded authority without anger, yet carried an indescribable weariness, as if an elder who had guarded too long had finally found someone to whom truth could be spoken. 'Or perhaps... the heir of the Seventh Chess Player.'

text.content: Deep within the Sea of Stars, a figure slowly coalesced. It was a middle-aged man in plain white robes, his features scholarly and elegant, yet his eyes held a detachment that suggested he had witnessed the rise and fall of all things. He stood with hands behind his back, stars revolving around him, as if the entire universe rested within his grasp. This was the ultimate Chess Player of the ancient game—Cang Yutian.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suppressed the churning emotions within him, his voice calmer than it had ever been: 'So from the very beginning, I was your chess piece? From the moment I obtained the Tianji Record Fragment in the ruins, everything was within your calculations?' He stared directly into those eyes that seemed capable of seeing through all things, a self-mocking curve at the corner of his lips, 'The ultimate Chess Master's chess game indeedcalculating every single move.'

Cang Yutian shook his head, and an uncommon bitterness appeared in his expression: 'A chess piece? No, you were never a chess piece.' He waved his hand, and scenes emerged from the surrounding Sea of Stars—countless shattered worlds, remnants devoured by the Void, the desperate wails of countless civilizations. 'Before the ancient times, there was no chess game. There was only a universe on the verge of being devoured by the Void, and a mad plan.'

text.content: In the vision, a solitary figure stood at the edge of the universe, facing the eternally churning darkness that devoured everything—the source of the Void. Cang Yutian's voice sounded within the scene: 'Order was born to resist the Void. The Tianji Record, the Prophets, the Chess Game... they were all a web of order I wove with my own hands. Without it, this universe would have completely perished ten thousand years ago.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, his gaze lingering on those remnants of the Void. He remembered some of the blurry images he had seen in the Tianji Record—those he had thought were merely ancient legends of shattered worlds, turned out to all be real. 'So your so-called protection means treating people as chess pieces? Making the Prophets exhaust their Heavenly Fate, making Chess Players destroy each other?' His voice turned abruptly cold, 'What kind of order is this?'

Cang Yutian did not become angry; instead, a rare approving smile appeared: 'Well said, Chen Ji. In ten thousand years, you are the first Chess Player to question me face to face.' He stepped forward, and the entire Sea of Stars trembled with him, 'But do you think I wanted this? Order has its price. Every Chess Player's rise means another's fall; every prophecy obtained is a透支 of the future. I simply chose the lesser evil among countless terrible options.'

text.content: Cang Yutian raised his hand, and a brilliant white light rose from his palm. That light was warm and serene, a stark contrast to the darkness of the Void. 'But now, I am tired. Ten thousand years is enough to erode any will. Order needs a new guardian.' His gaze fell upon Chen Ji, as if examining an artifact long awaited, 'The Tianji Record within you is nearly complete, and with the Seventh Chess Player's inheritance... you are the only one qualified to inherit all of this.'

dialogue.content: 'Inherit?' Chen Ji let out a cold laugh, 'Inherit your position, continue treating people as chess pieces? Continue making Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, and the others become consumables of order?' He stepped forward, and his aura actually faintly rivaled Cang Yutian's, 'You keep saying this is the only choice, yet you never asked those who were sacrificed whether they were willing. In these ten thousand years, has anyone asked those Prophets—whether they wanted to die?'

text.content: Cang Yutian fell silent for a moment, the light in his eyes dimming slightly. At this moment, he was no longer the lofty ultimate Chess Player, but an old man who had guarded for too long and was already exhausted. 'What good would asking do?' His voice was low, 'When the tide of the Void surges again, they would die just the same. Better to let part of the people go first than to have the entire universe perish together—that is the cruel essence of order.'

dialogue.content: He raised his hand again, and this time, the entire Sea of Stars began to converge toward his palm, countless stars forming a brilliant pillar of light connecting heaven and earth. 'But I give you another choice.' Cang Yutian's voice regained its authority, 'Inherit my position and become the new ultimate Chess Player. You will have the power to reshape order—abolish the Heavenly Fate consumption system, grant the Prophets true freedom, even...' He paused, 'Find a way to save your sister Chen Nian.'

text.content: The name 'Chen Nian' struck like a heavy hammer, brutally striking Chen Ji's heart. His pupils contracted sharply, that momentary loss of composure fully exposed. Cang Yutian seemed to have known all along, his smile deepening: 'Do you think the Holy Sect took her away merely for the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'? Her very existence is a threat to order—and now, this threat can become your strength.'

Chen Ji closed his eyes, countless scenes flashing rapidly through his mind. Su Qingyao's worries under the moonlight, Ye Qing's eyes that seemed cold yet actually yearned for freedom, Mo Xiansheng's expression of wanting to speak but holding back, and Chen Nian—his sister who had been missing for years, continuously appearing in the blurry prophecies of the Tianji Record, yet forever impossible to see clearly. If he accepted all this, could he truly change anything? Or would he become another Cang Yutian?

choice.prompt: Faced with Cang Yutian's proposal, Chen Ji fell into contemplation. His heart tore between anger and reason—acceptance meant becoming part of order, while refusal might allow everything to worsen. And that promise regarding Chen Nian...

choices.description: Become the new ultimate Chess Player and seek change from within the order. Although one might lose oneself, at least the people around can be protected.
choices.visible_cost: Lose free will and become part of order
choices.visible_reward: Gain the power to reshape order and save Chen Nian
choices.risk_hint: You may become another Cang Yutian

text.content: 'Very well.' Chen Ji opened his eyes, his voice terrifyingly calm, 'I accept. But I have conditions—abolish the Heavenly Fate consumption system and release all Prophets bound by order. And...' He paused, his gaze like a blade, 'Chen Nian must return safely.'

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian smiled faintly, and in that smile there was even a sense of relief: 'Deal.' He extended his hand, white light surging, 'From this day forward, you are the new ultimate Chess Player.'

choices.description: Refuse to be a continuation of order, choose to resist emptiness in your own way. The price is losing Cang Yutian's protection, but preserving the self.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the fastest way to save Chen Nian
choices.visible_reward: Retain independent will, unbound by order
choices.risk_hint: You will face the coming tide of emptiness alone
choices.process_label: decide to fight to the end

dialogue.content: "No." Chen Ji's answer was crisp and decisive. "I don't need to become you to find a way to save Chen Nian. As for emptiness..." A cold smile curled at the corner of his lips, the smile carrying a hint of madness. "For eons, everyone has been running circles within your order. Why can't someone carve out a new path?"

Cang Yutian's gaze changed for the first time—not with anger, but with pity: "You think a blaze of passion is enough to resist emptiness? The first Chess Player ten thousand years ago thought the same. His end, you should know clearly."

choices.description: Reject the deal but do not blindly resist. Propose cooperating with Cang Yutian to find a third path—neither yielding to the old order nor独自对抗虚无.
choices.visible_cost: The negotiation may fail, provoking Cang Yutian
choices.visible_reward: If successful, obtain partial order authority without losing freedom
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian may not accept the terms

dialogue.content: "I have one question." Chen Ji suddenly smiled, a smile that made Cang Yutian frown slightly. "You say order exists to resist emptiness, but why must it be in the form of a 'chess game'? Why not let the Prophet and the Chess Player know the truth and let them choose for themselves?"

Cang Yutian fell silent for a moment, then asked back: "You think I haven't tried?" His tone carried a hint of bitterness. "Prophets who know the truth collapse from fear; Chess Players who know the truth fall into despair. Order needs secrets, just as the human body needs pain—it is the instinct for survival."

text.content: However, at this very moment, the breath that had been dormant in Chen Ji for who knows how long suddenly erupted. A hoarse and furious voice exploded in his Mental Sea, the voice rough and desperate, as if carrying ten thousand years of hatred: "Cang Yutian! You hypocrite!"

Chen Ji's body trembled violently, a force not belonging to him was breaking through the seal. It was another layer of consciousness he had never detected—the remnant soul of the ancient Chess Player. He felt his consciousness being squeezed, the voice growing clearer: "Ten thousand years ago, you said the same thing! 'Inherit my position'—and then? Then you devoured all my companions, establishing this damnable order!"

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian's expression finally changed—it was a complex look of rage and terror mixed, as if his wounds had been ripped open: "You... how are you still alive?" His voice trembled for the first time. "You should have already..."

"Should already be dead?" The ancient voice was full of mockery. "Thanks to you, I've been trapped in the Tianji Record for ten thousand years, watching my successors be devoured by you one after another, becoming your eternal nourishment. Now, I've finally found someone who can hear my voice." The voice suddenly softened, as if speaking to Chen Ji. "Child, the person before you is the true enemy of the eternal chess game."

text.content: As Chen Ji was being bombarded by these two completely opposite messages until his head was splitting, he suddenly felt the seal on his chest completely shatter. A torrent of memories flooded into his mind—the final legacy left by the ancient Chess Player—about the true face of Cang Yutian, about another version of how the eternal chess game was established. In the images, Cang Yutian was no longer the guardian, but an ambitious schemer who, for the sake of eternity, did not hesitate to devour fellow practitioners and tamper with memories. The establishment of order, from the very beginning, was for his personal immortality.

choice.prompt: The ancient Chess Player's memories surged like a tide, fragments of truth gradually piecing together. Cang Yutian's true face seemed exposed, but Chen Ji was uncertain whether these memories were completely trustworthy—after all, the ancient Chess Player had also been trapped for ten thousand years; could his anger affect his judgment?

choices.description: The ancient Chess Player is the true victim, and his memories should be trustworthy. First oppose Cang Yutian, then verify the truth.
choices.visible_cost: May have fallen into manipulation by the ancient Chess Player
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the ancient Chess Player's complete power support
choices.risk_hint: You may just be another pawn being used

dialogue.content: "I believe you." Chen Ji murmured in his heart. In the next moment, he felt his consciousness merge with that ancient presence. His vision suddenly expanded, as if seeing an entirely new world. "Cang Yutian, it turns out you were a liar from the very beginning."

Cang Yutian's expression turned completely gloomy, the mask of compassion finally shattering to reveal the savagery beneath. "Since you insist on seeking death, I shall grant your wish. Ten thousand years is too long—I happen to need a final nourishment."

choices.description: You cannot fully trust words from either side. Pretend to make a choice while secretly seeking third-party verification—perhaps Mo Xiansheng knows something.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain a Neutral Position, Preserve All Possibilities
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian and the Ancient Chess Player May Simultaneously Develop Hostility Toward You

dialogue.content: "Two seniors," Chen Ji suddenly spoke, his voice terrifyingly calm. "You each argue your case—how am I supposed to distinguish the truth? One is a guardian who established order, the other a victim trapped within the Tianji Record for ten thousand years—who speaks falsehood?" A cold smirk curled at his lips. "Let me see for myself what this ancient chess game is truly about."

Cang Yutian and the Ancient Chess Player fell silent simultaneously. Chen Ji sensed a flicker of hesitation from that ancient consciousness, while a hint of wariness flashed in Cang Yutian's eyes. Neither had expected this seemingly young junior to maintain such composure in these circumstances.

text.content: Cang Yutian broke the silence first. His voice returned to calm, but the killing intent in those eyes could no longer be hidden. "Chen Ji, you're clever, but clever people often die the fastest." He stepped forward, and the entire star sea began to tremble. Countless stars transformed into blades suspended above Chen Ji's head. "Since you refuse to cooperate, I'll take action myself—retrieving both the Tianji Record and the inheritance of the Seventh Chess Player."

Yet at this moment, the runes of the Tianji Record suddenly blazed. A brilliant light erupted from Chen Ji's chest. Mo Xiansheng's familiar remnant soul figure appeared at his side—weak, yet carrying unwavering resolve. "Cang Yutian, did you think you were the only one playing the long game? For ten thousand years, I've guarded the first page of the Tianji Record, waiting precisely for this moment." His voice was hoarse, yet each word rang clear. "Chen Ji is not your chess piece—he never was. He is the breaker we all chose together."

Within the star sea, three forces formed a delicate standoff. Cang Yutian felt the pressure—he never imagined that a seemingly weak inheritor could unite so many hidden threads in such a short time. His plan had encountered variables for the first time. Chen Ji stood at the storm's center, observing all this, yet his heart was perfectly clear—regardless of the truth, he had no retreat. Ahead lay the abyss, behind the cliff, and he could only move forward.

"Fine, very fine." Cang Yutian suddenly smiled—that grin sinister and ice-cold. "It seems I've underestimated you ants." He spread his arms wide, and the entire star sea began to collapse. Countless stars transformed into a black tide surging toward Chen Ji. "Since the soft approach won't work, I'll use force! The ancient chess game was established by me, the rules set by me—before the Tianji Record, you have no chance of victory!"

At this critical moment, the ancient breath dormant within Chen Ji for millennia erupted. The Ancient Chess Player's voice thundered like a sudden clap, echoing across the entire star sea: "This is exactly what you said ten thousand years ago, Cang Yutian!" That voice was ancient and heroic, carrying boundless resentment and defiance. Simultaneously, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul ignited its final power, beginning to merge with the Ancient Chess Player's consciousness. Two remnant souls, three generations of chess players' wills, converged at this moment into a force capable of shaking heaven and earth, surging directly toward Cang Yutian!
